layers.note: A mat-forming plant of snowbeds and late-melting meadow slopes, often carpeting the ground where snow lies longest.

moisture.note: Moist ground under a late snowpack.

elevation_m.note: Low in Alaska; subalpine to alpine in the Washington Cascades.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −15 to 0 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 4 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −40 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 5 to 14 °C; gone below 3 °C, where summers are too short, and above 17 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 450 to 2,300 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 250.

degree_days_5.note: About 100 to 1,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 40.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.6, gone by 0.45.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Partridgefoot grows from Alaska and Yukon through British Columbia and the Cascades to northern California, and east to Alberta, Idaho and Montana (general range knowledge; not checked against PLANTS). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
